references.observation: This commit introduces the v0.5 native-speech change set and states that v0.4-and-earlier undeclared speech migrates as espeak while new v0.5 undeclared speech defaults to native.
normalize_project accepts project schemas v0.1 through v0.5, emits canonical schema v0.5, and chooses espeak for undeclared speech in older schemas while choosing native for v0.5.
The regression test_project_schema_migrates_legacy_speech_without_rewriting_its_engine checks that v0.4 undeclared speech normalizes to espeak and v0.5 undeclared speech normalizes to native.
The v0.8 changelog records the intended semantic split: new v0.5 speech defaults to native while v0.4-and-earlier undeclared speech migrates as espeak to preserve historical intent.
The v0.2 checkpoint changelog describes a v0.2 canonical schema alongside v0.1 compatibility; it does not describe a v0.1 project-state migration into v0.2.

The v0.2 canonical reader accepts both v0.1 and v0.2 project schemas and returns the incoming schema value in normalized state, grounding backward-reader compatibility rather than an automatic schema upgrade.
This full-SHA compare pins the bounded donor-history interval inspected between the admitted v0.1 and v0.2 checkpoints; the range defines search scope and is not itself proof that no migrator exists.

The checkpoint changelog states that lost uncommitted v0.3 source was rebuilt forward from surviving v0.1 source, the safe v0.2 branch, and v0.3 evidence rather than claimed as byte-for-byte recovery; it also records multi-version input compatibility.

This pinned canonical reader is evidence that older project schemas remain accepted by the later reader; reader acceptance alone does not demonstrate that the admitted v0.2 project artifact was transformed into a v0.4 artifact.

The recovery commit is explicitly titled as recovering and extending FrameState into a usable v0.4 video machine, and its changelog diff says the lost v0.3 body was rebuilt forward rather than resurrected byte-for-byte.

This full-SHA compare pins the bounded v0.2-to-v0.4 donor-history interval inspected for a project-state transformer, migration receipt, or derived target artifact; the range itself is only search-scope evidence.
The G1 handshake commit admits the host-side peer immediately after an authenticated HELLO/WELCOME exchange, providing the baseline admission semantics for the older generation.
The later handshake commit introduces protocol version 2 and requires an authenticated guest ACK before host admission, changing the admission state machine rather than adding a dual-stack bridge.
The regression commit checks that ACK is required before admission and that a protocol-version-1 HELLO is not admitted by the v2 host, grounding an explicit incompatibility boundary.

This full-SHA compare pins the bounded G1-to-G2 donor-history interval inspected for dual-stack negotiation, translation, or a migration receipt; the range does not prove universal absence outside that interval.
